nodes.label: Inference, breach and incident communication gap

nodes.label: Manual walkthroughs with versioned LLM prompts

nodes.label: First 50 eligible apps without category quotas

nodes.label: Missing privacy policies are included and reported

nodes.label: Unresolved post-harm reaction and accessibility

nodes.label: Two human coders and checklist walkthrough
nodes.description: Use checklist cognitive walkthrough and two coders; specify what they code and how.

nodes.label: LLM privacy-policy feasibility and pilot
nodes.description: Test LLM usability for policy analysis; pilot-informed choices are required but which procedures it evaluates remains unclear.

nodes.label: Unresolved best-app harm-tree synthesis

nodes.label: Citron and Solove 2022 Privacy Harms

nodes.label: Hudig and Singh 2025 fertility transparency
nodes.description: Suggested example of fertility-tracker transparency and control.

nodes.label: Malki et al. 2024 female mHealth privacy
nodes.description: Suggested example of post-Roe app privacy-practice analysis.

nodes.label: Salehzadeh Niksirat et al. 2024 wearable survey
nodes.description: Suggested entry point to utility, privacy and security literature for activity trackers.

nodes.label: Wharton et al. 1994 cognitive walkthrough
nodes.description: Method chapter in Usability Inspection Methods, pages 105–140, full Nielsen edited-volume PDF.

nodes.label: Provider communication of harms, stance and PET protection
nodes.description: Supervisor RQ asks which downstream privacy harms providers explicitly acknowledge/downplay and how technologies are framed as protective.

nodes.label: Historical document/interface study; survey optional
nodes.description: Proposal proceeds with document and interface analysis; user survey remains possible later phase, originally pending confirmation.

nodes.label: Tentative 2 November registration and 2 February deadline
nodes.description: Registration planned for 2026-11-02; official registration/deadline remain TODO. Twelve-week plan assumes 2027-02-02 deadline, not confirmed official dates.

nodes.label: Historical 1,000-rating floor and rating ranking
nodes.description: First 20 results per keyword, floor >=1,000 ratings, descending average rating then rating count; target 30/20 quota. Needs revision after 13 October.

nodes.label: Historical privacy-policy requirement
nodes.description: Sampling v1 requires reachable policy and excludes missing/dead policies after recording absence. Superseded by 13 October include-and-report rule.

nodes.label: Cross-store app unit and provider deduplication
nodes.description: App rather than listing is unit; cross-store matching uses developer, name, policy URL; repeated providers flagged for independence.

nodes.label: Pilot isolation from validation providers and documents
nodes.description: Five pilot apps remain in sample after recoding; validation avoids their providers/documents to prevent instrument-development leakage.

nodes.label: Historical per-source German-primary capture
nodes.description: Record language per source; German primary, English fallback. Superseded preference is English-first with details unresolved.

nodes.label: Capture date, version and SHA-256 provenance
nodes.description: Every app/source records stable app ID, capture date, version and SHA-256 file hash for traceability.

nodes.label: Source completeness and denominators
nodes.description: Distinguish captured, not offered, and exists-but-unretrieved sources; only failed retrieval reduces denominator under historical protocol.

nodes.label: Historical asymmetric recall validation
nodes.description: V1 prioritizes recall because false negatives manufacture silence; per-code kappa target .70 and no absence claims without measured recall.
nodes.rationale: Headline absence claims require reliable missed-mention detection.

nodes.label: Superseded blanket PET-origin limitation
nodes.description: V2 states PETs only remove implementation choices; v3 explicitly rejects this blanket rule and uses per-claim necessary conditions.

nodes.label: Harm baseline and definition
nodes.description: Harm is impairment/disruption of usual capacity; added study baseline is user situation without modelled pathway.

nodes.label: Harm tree: components, capabilities and harms
nodes.description: Three levels connect system components to actors capabilities/incapabilities and concrete negative consequences.

nodes.label: O-CORE, O-CTX and O-IMP component origins
nodes.description: Core functionality, digital context, implementation choices; literature-based origin arguments are not formal proofs.

nodes.label: Per-claim protection and necessary pathway conditions
nodes.description: A measure addresses pathway only by removing a necessary condition within claim scope; no blanket O-IMP restriction.

nodes.label: Planned domain reference harm trees
nodes.description: Before pilot, build versioned fitness/fertility trees from literature, with data, adversary, access, capability, consequence and AND/OR conditions.

nodes.label: App-by-pathway applicability records
nodes.description: Each pathway records feature evidence, access/context assumptions, applicable/not-applicable/uncertain decision and reason; uncertain rows counted.

nodes.label: RQ1 coverage: all mentioned nodes and modalities
nodes.description: Record every node asserted, possible or denied; maximum L-CMP/L-CAP/L-HRM level is derived summary.

nodes.label: L-GEN generic misuse risk
nodes.description: Generic misuse without concrete consequence is separate from L-HRM; inference features alone do not establish harm.

nodes.label: K-DIS, K-TRK, K-INF and K-INC capabilities
nodes.description: Distinguishing, tracking/profiling, inference and incapability; sensitive data collection alone is not inference.

nodes.label: Seven Knabenhans harm categories
nodes.description: Economic, physical, psychological, autonomy/deprivation, discrimination, reputational and societal harm.

nodes.label: T-REL relationship harm tag
nodes.description: Citron/Solove relationship damage tagged alongside applicable harm category, never replacing category.

nodes.label: P-BRC, P-INC and P-NOT breach/incident details
nodes.description: P-BRC user consequences of exposure; P-INC concrete incident response; statutory notification promises only P-NOT.

nodes.label: RQ2 stance attached to named harm
nodes.description: A named L-HRM harm may have several stances; component/capability-only units have none; absence is not stance.

nodes.label: S-ACK, S-QUA, S-MIN, S-RSP and S-DEN
nodes.description: Acknowledged, qualified, minimised, responsibility shifted, denied/prevented. Qualification alone is not minimisation; record qualification target.

nodes.label: RQ3 technical measures and N-COM commitments
nodes.description: Technical controls include T-3RD/T-INF/T-DEV/T-ENC/T-ANO/T-SEC/T-OTH; nontechnical commitments separate as N-COM; record actor/data/outcome/conditions.

nodes.label: F-FLW/F-HRM and partial/scoped/absolute protection
nodes.description: Code data-flow versus harm-prevention framing and strength; partial protection does not imply all remaining risk is prevented.

nodes.label: C-MIS potential mismatch: human review only
nodes.description: Claim-scope tension requires explanation of unaddressed necessary conditions. Author only, never model; no judgement of actual deployed system safety.

nodes.label: C-REA broad reassurance without named substance
nodes.description: Broad safety language without measure, scope or consequence; not applied when specific checkable measure named.

nodes.label: Paragraph or coherent UI block with evidence spans
nodes.description: List item keeps introduction; every positive code needs located quote; uncertain model output or missing span triggers manual review, not negative label.

nodes.label: Ten-app blind validation and leakage prevention
nodes.description: Ten apps, five per domain, random recorded seed, distinct pilot providers/documents, language stratification, fully hand-coded before seeing model output.

nodes.label: Per-code precision, recall, Cohen kappa and Gwet AC1
nodes.description: Correct label/unit/span; score staged pipeline end-to-end, app detection and provider-resampled exploratory intervals. These are planned metrics, not results.

nodes.label: Prompt paraphrases, recoding and second human review
nodes.description: Two paraphrased prompts, hidden label-source adjudication, two-app recoding >=two weeks later, second coder/supervisor review for applicability/minimisation/mismatch.

nodes.label: Lexical and outside-hit missed-mention audit
nodes.description: Read every unlabelled bilingual lexical hit plus 100 outside-hit units; fewer than 20 validation positives or recall <.90 triggers full manual checks or withholding absence claims.

nodes.label: Written ethics scope confirmation remains needed
nodes.description: Public documents and researcher throwaway-account walkthroughs usually have no human subjects; survey requires review. Obtain advisor/institution written guidance before recruitment.

nodes.label: Synthetic data and throwaway account walkthroughs
nodes.description: Never enter real health, identity or payment data; avoid real verification; check store terms before automation.
nodes.rationale: Protect researcher personal data and keep collection consistent with ethics constraints.

nodes.label: Walkthrough T1-T7 privacy goals and four questions
nodes.description: Seven tasks: collection, inference, breach/incident consequences, find policy, disable sharing, export, delete; inspect effect intent, action notice, action-effect association, progress feedback.

nodes.label: Neutral walkthrough outcomes and pilot limits
nodes.description: Completed, information not found, unsupported, access barrier with stopping location and question. Pilot fixes start point/time limit; do not anticipate failure.
nodes.rationale: Avoid analyst expectations steering inspection or treating time-bounded search as proven absence.

nodes.label: In-app UI evidence shares document codebook
nodes.description: Quote screen wording separately from interpretation; privacy text enters corpus as in_app_ui and same codebook.

nodes.label: Version every prompt and log exact model/runs
nodes.description: One task_vN.md per prompt with exact model, version, date, input/output schema and changes; log date, prompt, model, number documents and failures.

nodes.label: Study reproducibility and immutable captures
nodes.description: Record capture date/version, never edit collected raw artefact, version prompts/codebooks and validate LLM by random blind manual subsample.

nodes.description: parse_dom extracts script datasets and fixed positional fields without JavaScript execution or visible-label CSS extraction.

nodes.label: Observed absence versus scraper failure

nodes.rationale: Preserve parser and transport failure separately from observed negative findings.

nodes.label: Audited TLS verification defect
nodes.description: Pinned Python transport disables certificate verification globally and lacks explicit timeout; check script restores verified HTTPS.
nodes.rationale: Research source authenticity requires verified transport rather than inheriting unsafe defaults.

nodes.label: Constructed CycleMate example

nodes.label: Core context and implementation conditions
nodes.description: Reference tree distinguishes necessary core data, phone/network context and provider implementation choices using AND/OR logic.

nodes.label: App lock and backup pathway logic
nodes.description: App lock can block unlocked-phone access; disabling cloud backup does not close a seized-phone alternative; core cycle records cannot be removed while retaining function.
nodes.rationale: Protection blocks a pathway only by removing a necessary condition.

nodes.label: Synthetic applicability records
nodes.description: CycleMate F1/F3/F5 are applicable; legal-setting F2 and unconfirmed conditional-sharing F4 are uncertain and reported separately.

nodes.label: CycleMate v3 unit-level codes
nodes.description: Ten constructed units illustrate components, inference, named harms, stance, measures and reassurance, each supported by explicit spans.

nodes.label: Synthetic potential mismatches
nodes.description: On-device claim misses unlocked-phone pathway F1; encrypted predictions miss shared-identifier profiling F3; no-sale pledge does not promise to block those pathways.

nodes.label: Captured-material absence claim
nodes.description: No mention identified refers only to captured material and measured instrument limits; uncertain autonomy applicability is reported separately.
nodes.rationale: Avoid global provider-silence claims and separate missing communication from uncertain relevance.

nodes.label: Language model as evidence-span screener
nodes.description: LLM stages find spans, stance and protection; humans decide applicability/mismatches; blind ten-app validation requires matching label, unit and span.

nodes.label: Fictional App F proposal example
nodes.description: Constructed period tracker illustrates targeted-advertising harms and coding, explicitly describing no real app.

nodes.label: Pregnancy advertising harm pathway
nodes.description: Ad-SDK events, identifiers and repeated observations enable tracking/profiling; server records enable brokerage; either can cause psychological harm after pregnancy loss.

nodes.label: Scoped App F protection mismatch
nodes.description: No-sale pledge closes brokerage within its stated scope; withholding raw entries cannot guarantee no pregnancy ads when ad events/IDs or interest categories remain.
nodes.rationale: Mismatch tests the protection text against an in-scope pathway, not deployed-system safety.

nodes.label: RQ1 Coverage
nodes.description: Compare explicit data-flow, capability and harm mentions with applicable reference harms not found in captured material.

nodes.label: RQ2 Stance
nodes.description: Examine named harms acknowledged, qualified, minimised, denied or assigned to users.

nodes.label: RQ3 Protection
nodes.description: Examine claimed measures, benefits, strength and scope against the reference model.

nodes.label: RQ4 Communication surfaces
nodes.description: Compare policies, listings, marketing and inspected interfaces.

nodes.label: Provisional research gap
nodes.description: Initial review has not identified the combined harm-coverage, stance and PET-framing study in fitness/fertility; documented search must test this gap.

nodes.label: Literature-based privacy harm trees
nodes.description: Components lead to capabilities then possible harms; origins distinguish core functionality, digital context and implementation choices.

nodes.label: Cited GDPR and transparency context
nodes.description: Source discusses health/sex-life data, clear information duties, layered notices and consumer claims; thesis asks what providers communicate.

nodes.label: User prediction versus adversary capability
nodes.description: Planned method distinguishes an intended user prediction from an adversary obtaining or using it; protection depends on actor and conditions.
nodes.rationale: Inference features alone do not establish third-party access or prevention of possible harms.

nodes.label: Observed-practice disclosure precedents
nodes.description: Source summarises policy/network discrepancies and store-label studies; these precedents differ from the thesis's planned communication-of-harms analysis.

nodes.label: Risk communication literature
